items.title: Sideways, Not Up: Why AI Is Not a New Abstraction Layer
items.raw_excerpt: There is a popular claim that AI coding assistants are the next rung on the ladder of abstraction, sitting above high-level languages just as those languages sat above assembly. I take the strongest version of that argument seriously, then argue it does not hold. A compiler is a deterministic, specified, reproducible abstraction you can stop thinking about. An LLM is none of those things. It does not move us up the ladder so much as sideways into nondeterminism.

title_i18n.en: Sideways, Not Up: Why AI Is Not a New Abstraction Layer

excerpt_i18n.en: There is a popular claim that AI coding assistants are the next rung on the ladder of abstraction, sitting above high-level languages just as those languages sat above assembly. An LLM is none of those things. It does not move us up the ladder so much as sideways into nondeterminism.

items.title: Metric-Dependent Annotation Saturation for Learning from Label Distributions
items.raw_excerpt: When annotators disagree on a label, the disagreement itself carries signal—and the number of annotators needed to capture it depends on the evaluation metric. We fine-tune NLI models on label distributions subsampled from ChaosNLI, a dataset providing 100 independent annotator judgments per item, and identify metric-dependent saturation. items.title: Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels
items.raw_excerpt: LLM-as-a-judge panels aggregate votes from multiple models, with the expectation that diverse models yield more reliable evaluations. We develop a framework to measure the true informational value of such panels and quantify how far their reliability falls short of the independent-voting ideal. Testing a panel of 9 frontier LLMs from 7 model families on three natural language inference datasets (each with 100 human annotations per item), we find that the 9 judges effectively provide only about 2 independent votes’ worth of information. items.title: The Low-Tech AI of Elden Ring
items.raw_excerpt: The article discusses the low-tech AI design in Elden Ring, where enemy behaviors rely on simple finite state machines and scripts rather than complex machine learning, enhancing predictability and fairness for players.

title_i18n.en: The Low-Tech AI of Elden Ring
title_i18n.zh: 《艾尔登法环》的低技术人工智能
title_i18n.es: La IA de baja tecnología de Elden Ring

excerpt_i18n.en: The article discusses the low-tech AI design in Elden Ring, where enemy behaviors rely on simple finite state machines and scripts rather than complex machine learning, enhancing predictability and fairness for players.
excerpt_i18n.zh: 文章探讨了《艾尔登法环》中AI设计的低技术特性，指出其敌人行为模式相对简单，依赖有限状态机和预设脚本，而非复杂的机器学习。这种设计反而增强了游戏的可预测性和公平性，为玩家提供了清晰的策略空间。
